'''John Christopher''' "'''Charlie'''" '''Martin''' [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] (21 September 1926 &ndash; 22 March 1999) was a UK-born [[physicist]], known colloquially as "the father of Pulsed Power".<ref name=obit>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/obituary-charlie-martin-1085802.html |work=The Independent |title=Obituary: Charlie Martin |author=David Fishlock |date=8 April 1999 |access-date=9 October 2010}}</ref>

He was educated at [[King's College London|King's College, London]].<ref name=JCMPP>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9ORb4YQ6rlYC |title=J.C. Martin on pulsed power |author=John Christopher Martin |author2=Thomas H. Martin |author3=Arthur Henry Guenther |author4=Magne Kristiansen |publisher=Springer |isbn=0-306-45302-9 |year=1996 |access-date=9 October 2010}}</ref>

He was instrumental in the development of a US Nuclear Weapons Effects programme in the 1970s and received thanks in the history of the [[Defense Threat Reduction Agency|Defence Nuclear Agency]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dtra.mil/documents/aboutdtra/DefensesNuclearAgency.pdf |title=Defense's Nuclear Agency, 1947-1997 |publisher=DTRA History Series |page=238 |year=2002 |access-date=9 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611111956/http://www.dtra.mil/documents/aboutdtra/DefensesNuclearAgency.pdf |archive-date=11 June 2011 }}</ref> He was later awarded the Defence Nuclear Agency Gold Medal in 1977, one of only a few non-US citizens to receive it.<ref name=obit />

He was awarded the first ever [[Erwin Marx Award]] in 1981 at the third [[IEEE Nuclear and Plasma Sciences Society|IEEE International Pulsed Power Conference]] in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sandia.gov/ppc2005/history.html |title=Pulsed Power Conference History |access-date=9 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023055447/http://www.sandia.gov/ppc2005/history.html |archive-date=23 October 2013 }}</ref>
